# video27 - L1 proxy reconstruction (Three.js sampled-frame baseline) - round 001

Representation: L1 / proxy. Three.js sampled-frame baseline (not a Blender-equivalent protocol).

Observed in the 24 reference samples: one continuous in-car bumper-camera shot of a racing game on a mountain/lake circuit, no cuts. Speedometer readings (183 -> 52 -> 136 km/h) were used as the speed profile; the camera car brakes into a left turn, takes a slow right hairpin past Esso/Advan boards and yellow/black chevron boards, enters a long tunnel (~9.0 s to ~14.5 s), and a yellow rival car draws alongside on the image-left from ~12.4 s, stays alongside through the tunnel exit, and drops back out of view by ~18.2 s. The run ends in a grassy cutting with an overpass ahead.

Geometry: track built as a centreline integrated from turn segments keyed to traversal time, with a downhill grade profile (camera pitch follows the slope, matching the raised horizon in early samples). Road ribbon, white edge lines, red/white kerb ribbons, guardrails, chevron boards, grass verges, sloping terrain, forest/hill embankment ribbons, tunnel (ledges, walls, sloped haunches, ceiling, portals), overpass boxes, a lake disc, cone mountains, gradient sky dome. Signs are anchored from their observed image positions at specific sample times. Yellow car: box body, dark cabin, four wheel pivots that spin with travelled distance. Black pillarbox bars and the rear-view mirror housing are proxied with flat camera-attached panels; HUD text is not reproduced.

Camera: perspective, 55 deg vertical FOV, 1.0 m height, position = centreline + inferred lateral offset; yaw follows the road tangent plus lane-change heading; analytical, absolute-time sampling.

Inference (not observed): exact curve angles, radii, elevations, tunnel length, rival car longitudinal gaps between samples, scenery outside the frames.

Feedback received: none yet (initial round).

rounds.reason: Recalibrated camera FOV/height, rival car placement, tunnel and hairpin geometry from round-1 feedback.
